[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stanford Ignite: a four-week program designed to teach innovators how to formulate, develop, and commercialize their ideas.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] StartX: a non-profit startup accelerator that offers mentorship, office space, and funding to Stanford-affiliated entrepreneurs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stanford Venture Studio: a startup accelerator that provides resources and mentorship to students, alumni, and faculty members.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Design for Extreme Affordability: a year-long course in which interdisciplinary teams design products and services for underserved communities.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stanford Technology Ventures Program (STVP): a center for entrepreneurship education and research that offers courses, workshops, and resources to entrepreneurs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Startup Garage: a nine-month experiential course in which student teams design and launch their own startup.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] BASES Startup Career Fair: a yearly event that offers students the opportunity to connect with startups across various industries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Hacking for Defense: a course that teaches students how to use entrepreneurial principles to solve national security issues.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stanford Biodesign: a program that trains students in biomedical technology innovation and commercialization.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cardinal Ventures: a student-run venture fund that invests in Stanford-affiliated startups.
